la-subspace-01: Har set ke liye teen test: $0$ andar hai?, $+$ ke under closed?, scaling ke under closed? Dekho condition linear hai ya nahi, aur right side $0$ hai ya nahi.
Rule: homogeneous linear equation ($=0$) ka solution set aur koi bhi span hamesha subspace hota hai. Non-zero right side ($=1$) ya nonlinear condition ($xy=0$) usually fail karti hai.
Option (D) mein $(0,0,0)$ daalo: kya $0+0+0=1$? Phir $xy=0$ wale set ke do members dhoondo jinka sum set se bahar jaye. Trap: sirf $0$ check karke ruk jaana.
la-subspace-02: Chaaron sets pe same teen test: zero element andar?, sum andar?, negative scalar se multiply karke bhi andar? Words pe dhyan: $b\neq0$, $x_1\ge0$, invertible.
$Ax=b$ mein $x=0$ daalo: $A0=0$, kya ye $b$ ho sakta hai? Matrices wale options mein zero matrix check karo: kya wo symmetric hai, kya wo invertible hai?
$x_1\ge0$ test karo: $(1,0,0,0)$ ko $c=-1$ se multiply karo, kya $x_1\ge0$ bacha? Trap: sirf addition check karna aur negative scalars bhool jaana.
la-subspace-03: 'Always a subspace' poocha hai aur $b\neq0$ diya hai. Har option mein zero vector aur closure dono check karo; $\{0\}$ ko haath se jod dena kaafi nahi.
Closure test: $x,y$ set mein hain to $x+cy$ bhi hona chahiye. $Ax=0$ ke liye $A(x+cy)=Ax+cAy$ likho; $Ax=b$ ke liye $A(2x)$ compute karo; norm ball ke liye $2e_1$ dekho.
Option (C): agar $Ax=b$ to $A(2x)=2b$; kya $2b=b$ ho sakta hai jab $b\neq0$? Baaki options pe bhi yahi scaling test lagao. Trap: 'zero add kar diya to subspace ban gaya' sochna.
la-subspace-04: $W_k$ do linear equations se bana hai, par right side mein $k$ hai. Pehle dekho $(0,0,0)$ kis $k$ ke liye dono equations satisfy karta hai.
Solution set ka dim $=3-(\text{independent equations})$. $W_k$ = ek particular point + $W_0$ ki direction, yaani $W_0$ ki parallel shifted copy.
$W_0$ solve karo: $x+y=0$ se $y=-x$, aur $z=2x$; kitne free variables bache? Phir $W_3$ mein $x=3$ leke ek point nikalo. Trap: 'linear equations hain to hamesha subspace' sochna.
la-subspace-05: Polynomials bhi vectors hain; zero vector yahan zero polynomial hai. Har condition dekho: kisi linear operation ($p(1)$, $p'$) ko $0$ ke barabar rakhti hai, $1$ ke, ya degree pe hai?
Rule: $L(p)=0$ jahan $L$ linear ho (evaluation, derivative) to subspace; $L(p)=1$ ya 'degree exactly 2' usually fail. Har option mein zero polynomial daal ke shuru karo.
$p(0)=1$ wale set mein zero polynomial daalo: $p(0)=0$, kya ye $1$ hai? Degree-exact set ke liye $x^2$ aur $-x^2+x$ ka sum dekho. Trap: degree condition ko linear condition samajhna.
la-independence-01: Teen vectors $\mathbb{R}^3$ mein: dependent tab jab inse bana $3\times3$ matrix singular ho. To aisa $k$ chahiye jisse determinant zero ho.
Vectors columns mein: $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&k\end{pmatrix}=0$. First row se cofactor expansion: $1\cdot(\ldots)-0\cdot(\ldots)+1\cdot(\ldots)$.
Pehla term: $1\cdot(1\cdot k-0\cdot1)=k$. Teesra term $+1\cdot(1\cdot1-1\cdot0)$ nikalo, jodo aur $=0$ rakho. Trap: cofactor sign slip, ya sochna ki zero entry ($k=0$) se dependent ho jaata hai.
la-independence-02: Independence poore set ki property hai. Har statement ke key words dekho: '4 vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$', '$v_3\notin$ span', 'subset', 'zero vector'.
Rule: $c_1v_1+\dots+c_kv_k=0$ ka koi non-trivial solution ho to dependent. $\mathbb{R}^3$ ke vectors se bane matrix mein max 3 pivots; zero vector ke liye coefficient $1$ lekar dekho.

Statement (B): maan lo $c_1v_1+c_2v_2+c_3v_3=0$; case $c_3\neq0$ mein $v_3$ ko baaki do se express karo, kya contradiction aata hai? Case $c_3=0$ bhi socho. Trap: pairwise non-parallel ko independence samajhna.
la-independence-03: Har naya set $v_1,v_2,v_3$ ke combinations se bana hai. Asli sawal: kis set ka coefficient matrix singular hai?
Har naye vector ke coefficients ($v_1,v_2,v_3$ ke) ek row banao, phir $3\times3$ matrix ka det nikalo. Det $\neq0$ ⇒ independent, det $=0$ ⇒ dependent.
Option (D): rows $(1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,1,1)$, triangular, det $=1$. Baaki teen options ke matrices likho aur det check karo. Trap: sums aur differences ko ek jaisa samajhna, unke det alag hain.
la-independence-04: $5\times3$ matrix, rank $3$: rank columns ki sankhya ke barabar hai, par rows ki sankhya se kam. Har statement ko is fark se jodo.
Rank = independent columns ki max sankhya = independent rows ki max sankhya. Nullity $=3-\text{rank}$; aur $\operatorname{rank}(A^TA)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$, jahan $A^TA$ ka size $3\times3$ hai.
Rows: 5 rows hain par row space ka dim sirf 3, kya sab 5 independent ho sakti hain? Ab nullity nikalo aur $Ax=0$ wale statement pe lagao. Trap: rows aur columns ki baat mix karna.
la-basis-dim-01: Span ki dimension = kitne vectors sach mein independent hain. Pehle do coordinates dekho: $(1,2),(2,4),(0,0),(3,6)$, sab multiples hain; kuch vectors baaki ke combinations ho sakte hain.
Vectors ko rows bana ke row reduce karo: $R_2-2R_1$ aur $R_4-3R_1$. Jitni non-zero rows (pivots) bachen, utni dimension.
$R_2-2R_1=(0,0,1,1)$, jo bilkul $R_3$ hai. Ab $R_4-3R_1$ nikalo aur dekho wo bhi kisi row ke barabar hai kya. Trap: ek dependency pakad ke ruk jaana, ya bas vectors gin lena.
la-basis-dim-02: $W$ do linear equations se define hai, $\mathbb{R}^5$ ke andar. Solution set ki dimension = kitne variables free bachte hain.
$\dim W = n-(\text{independent constraints})$, yahan $n=5$. Check karo dono constraints independent hain: ek $x_1,x_2,x_3$ pe hai, doosra $x_4,x_5$ pe.
Pehli equation se $x_1=-x_2-x_3$, doosri se $x_4=x_5$. Ab gino kaunse variables apni marzi se choose ho sakte hain. Trap: constraints ki sankhya ko hi dimension bol dena.
la-basis-dim-03: $3\times3$ matrices ki poori space ka dim 9 hai. Har subset ke liye gino kitni entries tum freely choose kar sakte ho.
Symmetric: diagonal + upar wala part free, $n(n+1)/2$. Skew: $a_{ii}=-a_{ii}$ se diagonal $0$, $n(n-1)/2$. Trace $0$: 9 entries pe ek linear constraint.
Upper-triangular gino: row 1 mein 3, row 2 mein 2, row 3 mein 1 free entry. Ab $n=3$ daal ke baaki formulas nikalo. Trap: skew mein diagonal ko bhi free maan lena.
la-basis-dim-04: Har statement 'kitne vectors' aur 'span / independent' ke rishte pe hai. Yaad karo: spanning set kam se kam kitna bada, independent set zyada se zyada kitna bada ho sakta hai?
Rule: spanning set mein $\ge n$ vectors, independent set mein $\le n$. Exactly $n$ vectors hon to basis ke liye spanning ya independence mein se ek hi kaafi hai.

Option (A) test karo: $\mathbb{R}^2$ ($n=2$) mein kya ek akela vector poora plane span kar sakta hai? (D) ko 'subspace ka basis = 4 independent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^4$' se socho. Trap: count ignore karna.
la-basis-dim-05: 'Smallest possible' intersection poocha hai. Dono subspaces $\mathbb{R}^5$ ke andar hain, aur $3+4$ space ki dimension se zyada hai, isliye overlap zaroori hai.
Formula: $\dim(W_1\cap W_2)=\dim W_1+\dim W_2-\dim(W_1+W_2)$, aur $W_1+W_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^5$ isliye $\dim(W_1+W_2)\le 5$.
Intersection tab sabse chhota jab $\dim(W_1+W_2)$ sabse bada ho. Wo maximum value formula mein daalo. Trap: max/min ulta lena; $W_1\subseteq W_2$ wala case largest intersection deta hai.
la-special-matrices-01: $A^2=A$ (idempotent, yaani projection) aur $A\neq0, I$. Har statement ko is identity se prove karo, ya ek $2\times2$ counterexample se todo.
Eigenvalue: $Av=\lambda v$ pe $A$ do baar lagao, $A^2v=\lambda^2v$ aur $A^2v=Av=\lambda v$. Singular: agar $A^{-1}$ exist kare to $A^2=A$ ko $A^{-1}$ se multiply karke dekho.
$2A$ test: $(2A)^2=4A^2=4A$; kya ye $2A$ hai jab $A\neq0$? Symmetry ke liye $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ ka square nikalo. Trap: har projection ko symmetric (orthogonal) maan lena.
la-special-matrices-02: $N^k=0$ (nilpotent) aur $N\neq0$. Har statement ko eigenvalues se jodo, aur doubt ho to $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ jaise $2\times2$ example pe test karo.
$Nv=\lambda v$ se $N^kv=\lambda^kv$, aur $N^k=0$. $I+N$ ke eigenvalues $1+\lambda$ hote hain; aur symmetric matrix hamesha diagonalizable hoti hai.
Example $N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ lo: $N^2=0$ check karo, phir iska rank gino aur rank wale statement se compare karo. Trap: 'saare eigenvalues 0 hain to matrix zero hai' sochna.
la-special-matrices-03: $3\times3$ skew-symmetric, aur $3$ odd hai. Det ki do properties saath lagao: transpose se det nahi badalta, aur $-A$ ka det kya hota hai?
Rules: $\det A^T=\det A$ aur $\det(-A)=(-1)^n\det A$. Yahan $A^T=-A$, to $\det A=\det(A^T)=\det(-A)$ likho with $n=3$.
$(-1)^3$ ki value nikalo aur $\det A=(-1)^3\det A$ mein daalo; jo equation bane usse $\det A$ solve karo. Trap: $2\times2$ case ($\det=a^2$) ko $3\times3$ pe generalise kar dena.
la-special-matrices-04: 'Always true' poocha hai. Har expression ka transpose lo: wo khud ke barabar aaye to symmetric, minus khud aaye to skew-symmetric.
Rules: $(X+Y)^T=X^T+Y^T$, $(XY)^T=Y^TX^T$, $(A^T)^T=A$. Skew ke liye $A^T=-A$ daalo, symmetric ke liye $A^T=A$, $B^T=B$.
$(AB)^T=B^TA^T=BA$; kya $BA$ hamesha $AB$ hota hai? $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ se check karo. Trap: transpose mein order na palatna.
la-special-matrices-05: Idempotent $2\times2$ matrix (na $0$, na $I$) ke eigenvalues sirf $0$ aur $1$ hote hain. Trace aur det se is baat ko $k$ pe condition banao.
Eigenvalues $0,1$ ⇒ trace $=1$ aur $\det=0$. Yahan trace $=3+(-2)$, aur $\det A=3\cdot(-2)-k\cdot(-2)$.
$\det A=3\cdot(-2)-k\cdot(-2)$ simplify karo aur $0$ rakho, phir $A^2=A$ verify karo. Trap: $-k(-2)$ ko $-2k$ likhna, ya trace $=1$ pe ruk jaana; wo har $k$ ke liye true hai.
la-block-matrix-01: $M$ block upper-triangular hai, diagonal pe $I_2$. $(1,4)$ entry top-right block $B$ ke andar hai, to dekho $M^5$ mein woh block kaise badalta hai.
Blocks ko scalars ki tarah multiply karo (order rakh ke): $M^2=\begin{pmatrix}I&B\\0&I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}I&B\\0&I\end{pmatrix}$. Pattern se $M^k$ ka top-right block nikalo.
$M^2$ ka top-right $=I\cdot B+B\cdot I=2B$. Ab $M^5$ ka top-right block likho; $(1,4)$ entry us block ki $(1,2)$ entry hai. Trap: entry ko power 5 kar dena.
la-block-matrix-02: Block upper-triangular ka inverse bhi block upper-triangular hoga: $\begin{pmatrix}X&Y\\0&Z\end{pmatrix}$. Asli sawal sirf top-right $Y$ hai; sizes $p\neq q$ ho sakte hain, dhyan rakho.
$X=A^{-1}$, $Z=D^{-1}$ aate hain; ab $AY+BD^{-1}=0$ ko $Y$ ke liye solve karo (left se $A^{-1}$ lagao). Trap: order badalna; $D^{-1}BA^{-1}$ to $p\neq q$ pe defined hi nahi.
la-block-matrix-03: Neeche-left ka $2\times2$ block poora zero hai, to matrix block upper-triangular hai. Top-right block ($7,-1,5,9$) det pe koi asar nahi daalta.
Pehla block: $2\cdot3-1\cdot1=5$. Ab doosre block ka det $4\cdot1-1\cdot2$ nikalo aur multiply karo. Trap: block dets ko add karna, ya sirf top-left block le lena.
la-block-matrix-04: $AB$ ko chaar tarah dekh sakte ho: entries, columns, rows, outer products. Har statement mein sizes check karo: $a_i$ hai $m\times1$, $b_i^T$ hai $1\times p$.
Rule: row $i$ of $AB$ = (row $i$ of $A$)$\cdot B$; column $j$ of $AB$ = $A\cdot$(column $j$ of $B$); aur $AB=\sum_i(\text{column } i \text{ of } A)(\text{row } i \text{ of } B)$.
Option (B) ka size check karo: $b_i$ hai $p\times1$, $a_i^T$ hai $1\times m$, to $b_ia_i^T$ ka size kya? $AB$ ke size $m\times p$ se compare karo. Trap: outer product ka order ulta likhna.
la-block-matrix-05: Product $XY$ tabhi defined hai jab $X$ ke columns = $Y$ ke rows. Har option mein har adjacent pair ke inner sizes compare karo.
Sizes: $A$ $3\times2$, $B$ $2\times4$, $C$ $4\times3$. Har product ko $(r\times c)(r\times c)$ form mein likho aur beech ke do numbers match karo.
Option (A) $CAB$: $(4\times3)(3\times2)$ ok, result $4\times2$; phir $(4\times2)(2\times4)$ ok. Isi tarah baaki teen check karo. Trap: sirf pehla pair check karke chhod dena.
la-transpose-inverse-01: Har statement transpose/inverse ke ek rule ka test hai. Yaad rakho: product pe dono order ulta karte hain; sum pe inverse distribute nahi hota.
Rules: $(XY)^T=Y^TX^T$, $(XY)^{-1}=Y^{-1}X^{-1}$, $(X^T)^{-1}=(X^{-1})^T$. Sum wala claim $A=B=I$ jaise simple case pe test karo.
$A=B=I$ lo: $(A+B)^{-1}=(2I)^{-1}$ nikalo aur $A^{-1}+B^{-1}$ se compare karo. Phir $(AB^T)^T$ pe rule lagao with $X=A$, $Y=B^T$. Trap: inverse mein order na palatna.
la-transpose-inverse-02: $A^{-1}$ diya hai aur $(2A)^{-1}$ chahiye. $A$ nikalne ki zarurat nahi; bas socho scalar factor inverse ke andar se kaise bahar aata hai.
Verify karo $(2A)\cdot(\tfrac12A^{-1})=I$, phir $\tfrac12A^{-1}$ ki sirf $(1,1)$ entry nikalo. Trap: $(2A)^{-1}=2A^{-1}$ maan lena, ya ek entry ka reciprocal le lena.
la-transpose-inverse-03: Do operations hain: pehle transpose, phir inverse. Dono product ka order palat dete hain, to do baar palatne ke baad order kya hoga?
Step by step: $(AB)^T=B^TA^T$; phir $(XY)^{-1}=Y^{-1}X^{-1}$ lagao with $X=B^T$, $Y=A^T$; end mein $(A^T)^{-1}=(A^{-1})^T$.
Pehla step: $(AB)^T=B^TA^T$. Ab iska inverse likho, order dhyan se palat ke, aur options se match karo. Trap: order sirf ek baar palatna.
la-transpose-inverse-04: $A^2-3A+2I=0$ se $A$ ko ek taraf factor karo. Ye equation $A$ ke inverse aur eigenvalues ke baare mein batati hai, par $A$ ko poora fix nahi karti.
$A^2-3A=-2I$ ⇒ $A(A-3I)=-2I$, ya $A(3I-A)=2I$. Agar $AX=I$ mil jaye to $X=A^{-1}$; eigenvalues $\lambda^2-3\lambda+2=0$ follow karte hain.

$A(3I-A)=2I$ ko 2 se divide karo aur dekho $A^{-1}$ kaunsa expression hai; phir option (B) ka sign compare karo. (A) ke liye $\operatorname{diag}(1,2)$ try karo. Trap: terms move karte waqt sign slip.
la-transpose-inverse-05: $A$ invertible hai aur $c\neq0,1$. Har statement ko seedha multiply karke check karo: kya (claimed inverse) × (matrix) $=I$ aata hai?
(C) ko $c=2$ pe test karo: $(2A)(2A^{-1})$ kya deta hai? (B) ke liye $A^2(A^{-1})^2=AAA^{-1}A^{-1}$ simplify karo. Trap: scalar ko inverse mein waisa hi chhod dena.
la-rank-rref-01: Rank = row reduce ke baad kitni non-zero rows bachti hain. $R_2$ seedha $R_1$ ka multiple dikhta hai; $R_4$ ko bhi dhyan se dekho.
Operations: $R_2-2R_1$, $R_4-R_1$, phir naye $R_4$ ko $R_3$ se compare karo. Jo non-zero rows bachen aur independent hon, unki ginti = rank.
$R_2-2R_1=(0,0,0,0)$. Ab $R_4-R_1$ nikalo aur $R_3=(0,1,1,0)$ se compare karo. Trap: sirf multiples dhoondhna; ek row do rows ka sum bhi ho sakti hai.
la-rank-rref-02: $3\times4$ matrix, to rank max 3. Pehle teen columns mein $R_3=R_1+R_2$ jaisa dikhta hai, par har entry check karni padegi, last column bhi.
Row reduce: $R_2-2R_1$ aur $R_3-3R_1$, phir in dono naye rows ko ek doosre se subtract karo. Pivots gino.
$R_2-2R_1=(0,1,1,1)$. Ab $R_3-3R_1$ nikalo aur isse compare karo: kya difference zero row hai? Trap: $R_1+R_2=(3,7,4,1)$ ko $R_3$ maan lena; last entry alag hai.
la-rank-rref-03: $k$ sirf last entry mein hai. Rows 1 aur 2 multiples nahi hain, to rank kam se kam 2; sawal ye hai ki kis $k$ pe teesri row gayab hoti hai.
Eliminate: $R_2-R_1$, $R_3-R_1$, phir $R_3-2R_2$. Last row $(0,0,\text{kuch } k \text{ mein})$ bachegi; wo zero kab hoti hai?
$R_2-R_1=(0,1,2)$ aur $R_3-R_1=(0,2,k-1)$. Ab $R_3-2R_2$ ki third entry nikalo aur zero rakho. Trap: $R_3-R_1$ mein $k$ se 1 ghatana bhool jaana.
la-rank-rref-04: 'Always true' poocha hai. Har rank identity ko proof se, ya ek chhote counterexample ($I$, $-I$, $B=0$) se test karo.
Facts: row rank = column rank; $A^TAx=0\Rightarrow x^TA^TAx=\lVert Ax\rVert^2=0$; sum ke liye sirf $\le$; aur $\operatorname{rank}(AB)\le\min(\operatorname{rank}A,\operatorname{rank}B)$.
(A) ko $A=I$, $B=-I$ pe test karo: $A+B$ ka rank kya? (D) mein $B=0$ lo (wo bhi square hai) aur $AB$ ka rank dekho. Trap: 'square' ko 'invertible' samajh lena.
la-rank-rref-05: Entries $a_{ij}=i+j$: pehle matrix likho, rows $(2,3,4,5),(3,4,5,6),\dots$. Har agli row pichli se ek fixed vector se badhti hai.
Row reduce: $R_2-R_1$, $R_3-R_1$, $R_4-R_1$ karo, aur har difference ko $(1,1,1,1)$ se compare karo.
$R_2-R_1=(1,1,1,1)$, $R_3-R_1=(2,2,2,2)$. Ab $R_4-R_1$ nikalo, phir gino kitni independent rows bachi ($R_1$ ko mat bhoolna). Trap: 'difference same hai to sab rows ek hi row ke multiples' sochna.
la-rank-nullity-01: $5\times7$ matrix: $A$ $\mathbb{R}^7$ se $\mathbb{R}^5$ mein map karta hai. Null space $\mathbb{R}^7$ ke andar rehta hai, to columns ki ginti matter karti hai.
Rank–nullity: rank + nullity $=n$, jahan $n$ = columns ki sankhya $=7$. Rank $=3$ diya hai.
Equation likho: $3+\text{nullity}=7$, aur nullity solve karo. Trap: rows wala $5$ use kar lena; $5-\text{rank}$ to $A^T$ ki nullity hoti hai.
la-rank-nullity-02: $A$ ki nullity di hai, $A^T$ ki chahiye. Dono ko jodne wali cheez rank hai: $A$ aur $A^T$ ka rank same hota hai, nullity nahi.
Do steps: $\operatorname{rank}A=6-\text{nullity}(A)$ ($A$ ke 6 columns). Phir $A^T$ ($6\times4$, yaani 4 columns) pe: nullity$(A^T)=4-\operatorname{rank}$.
Pehla step: $\operatorname{rank}A=6-3=3$. Ab yahi rank $A^T$ ke 4 columns wale rank–nullity mein lagao. Trap: maan lena ki $A^T$ ki nullity bhi $3$ hai.
la-rank-nullity-03: $3\times5$ wide matrix: 5 columns, sirf 3 rows. Rank zyada se zyada 3 ho sakta hai; yahi one-to-one aur onto dono decide karta hai.
One-to-one ⇔ nullity $=0$; onto $\mathbb{R}^3$ ⇔ rank $=3$. Rank–nullity: nullity $=5-\operatorname{rank}$, aur $\operatorname{rank}\le3$.
Sabse kam nullity tab jab rank max ho: $5-3$ nikalo. Ab check karo kya nullity 0 ho sakti hai, aur kya '$\ge3$' guaranteed hai. Trap: rank ko 2 maan ke $5-2$ lena.
la-rank-nullity-04: $A$ already row-echelon form mein hai: pivots columns 1 aur 3 mein. Koi vector null space mein hai ya nahi, wo seedha $Ax$ compute karke check karo.
Free variables $x_2,x_4$. Row 2: $x_3+3x_4=0$; row 1: $x_1+2x_2-x_4=0$. Nullity = columns − pivots.
$(1,0,3,1)$ ko row 2 mein daalo: $x_3+3x_4=3+3$, kya ye zero hai? Ab $(-2,1,0,0)$ ko dono rows mein daalo. Trap: $x_3=-3x_4$ mein sign slip.
la-rank-nullity-05: $A^2=0$ ka matlab $A(Ax)=0$ har $x$ ke liye: $A$ ka har output wapas $A$ ke null space mein girta hai. $A\neq0$ bhi diya hai.
Column space $\subseteq N(A)$, to $\operatorname{rank}A\le\text{nullity}(A)=3-\operatorname{rank}A$. Is inequality se rank pe bound nikalo.
$\operatorname{rank}A\le3-\operatorname{rank}A$ solve karo, aur $A\neq0$ se rank $\ge1$ lagao; phir nullity $=3-\operatorname{rank}$. Trap: rank ko hi nullity bol dena, ya $A^2=0$ ko $A=0$ samajhna.
la-solvability-01: $3\times5$, rank 3: rank rows ki sankhya ke barabar, par columns se kam. Existence rows se judi hai, uniqueness columns se.
Rule: rank $=m$ (rows) ⇒ har $b$ ke liye solution exists; rank $=n$ (columns) ⇒ at most one solution. $A^T$ ($5\times3$) ke liye $m,n$ swap ho jaate hain.
Nullity of $A$ $=5-3$ nikalo: agar ye $>0$ hai to ek solution mein null vector jodne se kya hota hai? Phir $A^T$ ki nullity $3-3$ dekho. Trap: existence aur uniqueness mix karna.
la-solvability-02: $5\times3$, rank 3: rank columns ki sankhya ke barabar, par rows (5) se kam. Ye tall matrix hai; normal equations ($A^TA$) wale option pe bhi dhyan do.
Rank $=n$ ⇒ $N(A)=\{0\}$, solution ho to unique. Rank $<m$ ⇒ column space $\mathbb{R}^5$ ka sirf 3-dim hissa. Aur $\operatorname{rank}(A^TA)=\operatorname{rank}A$, size $3\times3$.
$A^TA$ ka rank 3 aur size $3\times3$: kya ye invertible hai? Phir socho 3-dim column space kya poora $\mathbb{R}^5$ cover kar sakta hai. Trap: uniqueness ko existence samajh lena.
la-solvability-03: Infinitely many solutions ke liye coefficient matrix singular ho aur system consistent rahe. Left sides dekho: teesri equation pehli do ka combination lagti hai.
Augmented matrix row reduce karo: $R_2-R_1$, $R_3-R_1$, phir $R_3-2R_2$. Last row $(0,0,0\,|\,\ldots)$ banegi; consistent ke liye uska right side zero chahiye.
$R_2-R_1=(0,1,2\,|\,8)$ aur $R_3-R_1=(0,2,4\,|\,m-6)$. Ab $R_3-2R_2$ ka right side likho aur zero rakho. Trap: right side combine karte waqt sign slip, ya teesre ka right side doosre jaisa maan lena.
la-solvability-04: $k$ sirf coefficient mein hai, right sides $3$ aur $6$ fixed. Pehle dekho kis $k$ pe coefficient matrix singular hai, phir us case mein right side check karo.
$\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&k\end{pmatrix}=k-4$. Det $\neq0$ ⇒ unique; det $=0$ pe rank $A$ aur rank $[A|b]$ compare karo.
$k=4$ daalo: doosri equation $2x+4y=6$ ban jaati hai; kya ye pehli ka exact multiple hai, right side samet? Trap: singular dekhte hi 'no solution' maan lena.
la-solvability-05: Elimination ho chuka hai: last row poori zero hai, pivots columns 1, 2 mein. Har option ko equations mein daal ke, ya rank se judge karo.
Equations: $x+2z=3$, $y-z=1$, $z$ free. Consistent ⇔ koi $(0\;0\;0\,|\,c\neq0)$ row nahi; rank $<3$ unknowns ho to infinitely many.
$(1,0,1)$ test karo: $x+2z=1+2$ theek, ab $y-z=0-1$ check karo. Phir $z=0$ rakh ke $x,y$ nikalo aur option (A) se milao. Trap: $y-z=1$ mein sign slip.
la-solvability-06: Sirf $z$ chahiye, poora solution nahi. Elimination se pehle $x$ hatao, phir $y$, taaki ek equation sirf $z$ mein bache.
$x$ hatao: $R_2-2R_1$ aur $R_3+R_1$ (kyunki $R_3$ mein $-2x$ hai). Phir in do naye equations se $y$ eliminate karo.
$R_2-2R_1$: $y+3z=11$. $R_3+R_1$: $2y+3z=13$. Ab doosri mein se pehli ka double ghatao aur $z$ nikalo. Trap: back-substitution ke baad $y$ ya $x$ report kar dena.
la-rank-rref-06: Rows 3 aur 4 ko pehli do rows se compare karo: kya ye $R_1, R_2$ ke sum/difference jaise dikhte hain? Rank pata chale to nullity rank–nullity se aayegi.
Check karo $R_3-R_1-R_2$ aur $R_4-R_1+R_2$ zero rows hain kya. Phir nullity $=4-\operatorname{rank}$ (4 columns).
$R_1+R_2=(1,1,3,0)$; isko $R_3$ se compare karo. Ab $R_1-R_2$ nikalo aur $R_4$ se milao. Trap: 'rows 3 aur 4 ek doosre ke multiple nahi, to independent' sochna.
la-det-props-01: Do rules ek saath: scalar $2$ poore $3\times3$ matrix pe laga hai, aur andar inverse hai. Pehle alag karo kya scale ho raha hai aur kya invert.
$\det(2A^{-1})=2^3\cdot\det(A^{-1})$; $2^3=8$, ab ise $\det(A^{-1})$ se multiply karo. Trap: $2^3$ ki jagah sirf $2$ lena, ya ise $(2A)^{-1}$ samajh lena.
la-det-props-02: Do cheezein: $-3$ poore $4\times4$ matrix ko multiply kar raha hai, aur $A^T$ hai. Size $n=4$ power mein jaayega.
Pehle $(-3)^4$ nikalo; even power hai to sign kya hoga? Phir $\det(A^T)$ se multiply karo. Trap: power $3$ le lena, ya $\det(A^T)=-\det A$ maan lena.
la-det-props-03: 'Always true' poocha hai; har statement ek determinant rule hai. Row operations ke teen types (swap, scale, add multiple) alag-alag effect dete hain.
Rules: row swap ⇒ $\times(-1)$; ek row ko $c$ se scale ⇒ $\times c$; ek row mein doosri ka multiple jodna ⇒ koi change nahi. Aur $\det(AB)=\det A\det B$.
(B) ko $A=B=I_2$ pe test karo: $\det(2I_2)$ nikalo aur $1+1$ se compare karo. (C) ke liye dono sides ko $\det A\cdot\det B$ ke form mein likho. Trap: 'add multiple' ko 'scale' samajhna.
la-det-props-04: Teen row operations ek-ek karke hue hain. $\det A=5$ se shuru karo aur har operation ke baad det track karo.
Ek row ko 3 se multiply ⇒ det $\times3$ (not $3^3$); swap ⇒ $\times(-1)$; ek row mein doosri row ka multiple jodna ⇒ koi change nahi.
Step (i) ke baad: $5\times3=15$. Ab steps (ii) aur (iii) ka effect lagao. Trap: single row scaling ke liye $3^3$ lena, ya swap ka sign bhool jaana.
la-det-props-05: $\operatorname{adj}A$ ka det poocha hai, $A$ $3\times3$ hai. Adjugate ko $A$ aur $\det A$ se jodne wali identity yaad karo.
$A\cdot\operatorname{adj}A=(\det A)I_3$. Dono sides ka det lo: $\det A\cdot\det(\operatorname{adj}A)=\det\big((\det A)I_3\big)$.
Right side: $\det(cI_3)=c^3$ with $c=\det A=3$. Ab dono sides ko $\det A$ se divide karo. Trap: power $n$ hi rakh dena; divide karne ke baad power $n-1$ bachti hai.
la-det-poly-01: $\det(A^2+I)$ chahiye aur eigenvalues diye hain. $A^2+I$ ke eigenvalues $A$ ke eigenvalues se seedhe nikalte hain; det unka product hai.
Har eigenvalue pe $p(\lambda)=\lambda^2+1$ lagao, phir $\det(A^2+I)=p(1)\cdot p(2)\cdot p(-1)$.
$p(1)=1+1=2$. Ab $p(2)$ aur $p(-1)$ nikalo (dhyan: $(-1)^2=+1$) aur teeno multiply karo. Trap: $\det A$ ko polynomial mein daalna, ya values add kar dena.
la-det-poly-02: Polynomial $\lambda^2-5\lambda+6$ ko dhyan se dekho aur diye gaye eigenvalues $2, 3$ se compare karo.
$\det p(A)=p(2)\cdot p(3)$ jahan $p(\lambda)=\lambda^2-5\lambda+6$. Polynomial ko factor bhi kar sakte ho.
$p(\lambda)$ ko $(\lambda-a)(\lambda-b)$ form mein factor karo, phir $\lambda=2$ aur $\lambda=3$ daal ke product lo. Trap: $\det A=6$ ko $p$ mein daalna, ya det ko sum pe tod dena.
la-det-poly-03: $\det(A^{-1}+2I)$: pehle $A^{-1}$ ke eigenvalues socho, phir $+2I$ ka effect, phir sabka product.
$\lambda=1$: $1+2=3$. $\lambda=-2$: $-\tfrac12+2=\tfrac32$. Ab $\lambda=3$ wala nikalo aur teeno multiply karo. Trap: $1/\det A+2$ lagana, ya $1/\lambda$ ki jagah $-\lambda$ lena.
la-det-poly-04: Sirf trace aur det diye hain, $A$ nahi. $\det(A-I)$ asal mein characteristic polynomial ki value hai ek khaas point pe.
$\chi(t)=\det(A-tI)=t^2-(\operatorname{tr}A)t+\det A=t^2-5t+6$, aur $\det(A-I)=\chi(1)$. Ya eigenvalues nikal ke $\prod(\lambda_i-1)$ lo.
Eigenvalues: aise do numbers socho jinka sum $5$, product $6$. Ab har ek mein se 1 ghata ke multiply karo. Trap: $\det A-\det I$ karna; det linear nahi hai.
la-det-poly-05: $A^2+A$ ek polynomial in $A$ hai, to $\det(A^2+A)$ = har eigenvalue pe $\lambda^2+\lambda$ ka product. $\det A$ seedha polynomial mein mat daalo.
$p(1)=1+1=2$, $p(-2)=4-2=2$. Ab $p(2)$ nikalo aur teeno ka product lo. Trap: values add karna, ya $(\det A)^2+\det A$ lagana.
la-eig-trace-det-01: Do eigenvalues pata hain ($3$, $3$), teesra chahiye. Trace nikalna easy hai; diagonal entry $4$ eigenvalue nahi, kyunki matrix triangular nahi hai.
Diagonal jod ke trace nikalo aur equation $\lambda_3$ ke liye solve karo. Cross-check: $A(1,1,1)^T$ compute karo, kya ye $(1,1,1)^T$ ka multiple hai? Trap: trace se $3$ sirf ek baar ghatana.
la-eig-trace-det-02: Matrix triangular nahi hai, to diagonal $1, 2$ eigenvalues nahi hain. $2\times2$ ke liye trace aur det se characteristic equation seedha banti hai.
Trace $=3$, det $=-4$: equation $\lambda^2-3\lambda-4=0$. Ab factor karo, ya options mein sum $=3$ aur product $=-4$ check karo. Trap: trace aur det ko hi eigenvalues bol dena.
la-eig-trace-det-03: Matrix dekho: diagonal ke upar sab zero hai, yaani $A$ lower triangular hai. Har option alag judge karo; D mein $A+A^T$ ki shape badal jaati hai.
Triangular matrix ke eigenvalues = diagonal entries, $\det$ = unka product. Diagonalizable ke liye repeated $\lambda=3$ ka GM $=3-\operatorname{rank}(A-3I)$ nikaal ke AM se compare karo.
$A-3I=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&0\\5&0&0\\-1&4&0\end{pmatrix}$ ka rank gino. Trap: $A+A^T$ triangular nahi hai, to uska diagonal $4,6,6$ eigenvalues nahi deta; $\det(A+A^T-4I)$ check karke dekho.
la-eig-trace-det-04: Teen eigenvalues mein se ek ($2$) diya hai; baaki do ke liye trace aur det se do equations mil jaati hain.
Ab $t^2-(\text{sum})t+(\text{product})=0$, yaani $t^2-t-6=0$ solve karo aur teeno mein smallest chuno. Trap: $-6$ ya $1$ khud eigenvalue nahi — wo baaki do ka product aur sum hain.
la-eig-trace-det-05: $B$ triangular nahi hai (dono off-diagonal entries non-zero), to diagonal $5,2$ ko seedha eigenvalues mat maano. Har option alag check karo.
2×2: $\lambda^2-(\text{tr})\lambda+\det=0$; yahan tr $=7$, det $=5\cdot2-4\cdot1=6$. Eigenvector check: $Bx$ nikaalo aur dekho wo $x$ ka multiple hai ya nahi.

$\lambda^2-7\lambda+6=0$ factor karo; option A ke liye $B(4,1)^T$ ka pehla component $5\cdot4+4\cdot1$ nikaalo. D: $B-I$ singular tabhi jab $1$ eigenvalue ho. Trap: candidate pair ko trace aur det dono se cross-check karo.
la-eig-transform-01: Sirf eigenvalues $1,2,-3$ diye hain, matrix nahi. Har option ek transformed matrix ($A^{-1}$, $A+2I$, $3A$, $A^2$) ke baare mein hai — ek-ek eigenvalue transform karke check karo.
Rule (same eigenvectors): $\lambda\mapsto1/\lambda$, $\lambda+2$, $3\lambda$, $\lambda^2$. Aur $\det(cA)=c^n\det A$, yahan $n=3$, $\det A=1\cdot2\cdot(-3)=-6$.
Option C: $3A$ ke eigenvalues $3\cdot1,\,3\cdot2,\,3\cdot(-3)$ — inka product khud nikaal ke $-162$ se milao. Trap: $\det(3A)=3\det A$ nahi, $3^3\det A$ hota hai; aur $(-3)^2$ ka sign dhyan se.
la-eig-transform-02: $\operatorname{tr}(A^3)$ chahiye par matrix nahi diya, sirf eigenvalues $2,-1,3$. Trace = eigenvalues ka sum, to pehle $A^3$ ke eigenvalues socho.
$2^3=8$, $3^3=27$; ab $(-1)^3$ ka sign dhyan se lagao aur add karo. Trap: $(\operatorname{tr}A)^3=4^3$ mat karo — trace power ke saath multiplicative nahi hai.
la-eig-transform-03: $A^{-1}$ ka trace chahiye. Trace eigenvalues ka sum hai, to pehle socho $A^{-1}$ ke eigenvalues $2$ aur $4$ se kaise bante hain.
$A^{-1}$ ke eigenvalues $1/\lambda_i$ hain (same eigenvectors), isliye $\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1})=\frac1{\lambda_1}+\frac1{\lambda_2}$ with $\lambda=2,4$.
$\tfrac12$ aur $\tfrac14$ ko common denominator $4$ pe add karo. Trap: $1/(2+4)$ (trace ka inverse) ya $1/\det A=1/8$ — dono galat hain.
la-eig-transform-04: $v$ pehle se $A$ ka eigenvector hai; sawaal hai ki $B=(A-2I)^{-1}$ usi $v$ pe kya karta hai. Shift aur inverse kis order mein lage hain, ye dhyan se dekho.
Pehle $(A-2I)v=Av-2v$ ko $\lambda$ ke terms mein likho, phir dono side pe $B$ lagao, kyunki $B(A-2I)=I$.
$(A-2I)v=(\lambda-2)v$. Ab dono side $B$ se multiply karo aur $Bv$ ke liye solve karo ($\lambda\neq2$). Trap: pehle invert karke phir $2$ ghatana ($1/\lambda-2$) galat order hai.
la-eig-transform-05: $(A-4I)^2$ ke teeno eigenvalues nikaalne padenge — sirf $A$ ke largest eigenvalue $3$ ko transform karna kaafi nahi.
Map $\lambda\mapsto(\lambda-4)^2$ har eigenvalue $1,2,3$ pe lagao (same eigenvectors).
$\lambda=3$ se $(3-4)^2=1$ milta hai; ab $\lambda=1$ aur $\lambda=2$ ke liye bhi nikaalo aur compare karo. Trap: yeh map yahan increasing nahi — jo $\lambda$ $4$ se sabse door, wahi bada banega.
la-rank-one-01: $A=uv^T$ outer product hai, to har column $u$ ka multiple hai — rank-one structure. Har option ko isi structure se judge karo.
$v^Tu=2\cdot1+(-1)\cdot2+1\cdot2$ compute karo, phir A aur B ko isse match karo. Trap: non-zero eigenvalue $v^Tu$ hai, $\lVert u\rVert^2=u^Tu$ nahi.
la-rank-one-02: $I_3+xx^T$ = identity + rank-one matrix. Determinant = eigenvalues ka product, to $I+xx^T$ ke eigenvalues socho.
Rule: $xx^T$ ke eigenvalues $x^Tx,0,0$; $I$ jodne se har eigenvalue mein $+1$, yaani $1+x^Tx,\,1,\,1$.
$x^Tx=1^2+1^2+2^2=6$; ab teeno eigenvalues likho aur multiply karo. Trap: teeno eigenvalues $1+x^Tx$ nahi hain, aur $+1$ bhoolna bhi galat hai.
la-rank-one-03: Rank-one $uv^T$ ki saari kahani $v^Tu$ pe tiki hai — pehle wahi number dekho, yahan kuch special ho sakta hai.
Eigenvalues $v^Tu,0,0$ aur $A^2=(v^Tu)A$. Diagonalizable ke liye GM$(0)=3-\operatorname{rank}A$ ko AM$(0)$ se compare karo.
$v^Tu=1\cdot1+1\cdot(-1)+0\cdot3$ compute karo, phir socho $A^2$ kya banta hai. Trap: $\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert$ singular value hai, eigenvalue nahi.
la-rank-one-04: $J$ (sab entries 1) $=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^T$, ek rank-one matrix hai. $\det(J+2I)$ = $J+2I$ ke eigenvalues ka product.
$\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^T$ ke eigenvalues $\mathbf 1^T\mathbf 1=5$ aur $0$ (4 baar). $+2I$ har eigenvalue mein $2$ jodta hai.
Toh $J+2I$ ke eigenvalues: ek $5+2$ aur chaar $0+2$; ab product nikaalo. Trap: sabko $7$ maan lena, ya $J$ ignore karke sirf $2^5$ lena.
la-rank-one-05: Wahi $u,v$ wala rank-one $A=uv^T$; $A^{10}$ ka trace chahiye — 10 baar multiply mat karo, eigenvalues use karo.
$v^Tu=2\cdot1+(-1)\cdot2+1\cdot2$ compute karo, phir uski 10th power lo. Trap: $A^{10}=(v^Tu)^9A$ use karo to $\operatorname{tr}A$ se multiply karna mat bhoolo.
la-rank-gm-01: GM = eigenvalue $2$ ke eigenspace ka dimension. Diagonal pe teeno $2$ hain (AM 3), par upar wala $1$ GM ko kam kar sakta hai.
GM $=n-\operatorname{rank}(A-2I)$ with $n=3$. $A-2I$ likho: sirf $(1,2)$ entry $1$ bachti hai, baaki sab zero.
$A-2I=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ ka rank gino, phir $3$ se ghatao. Trap: rank khud GM nahi hai, aur GM ko AM ke barabar mat maano.
la-rank-gm-02: Chaaron matrices triangular hain, to eigenvalues diagonal pe hi dikh rahe hain. Jahan eigenvalue repeat hota hai, wahan asli test GM vs AM hai.
Distinct eigenvalues ho to matrix hamesha diagonalizable. Repeated $\lambda$ ke liye GM $=2-\operatorname{rank}(A-\lambda I)$ nikaalo; GM = AM chahiye.

Option A: $A-2I=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ ka rank dekho aur GM nikaalo; C ka structure bhi aisa hi hai. Trap: repeated eigenvalue ka matlab automatically non-diagonalizable nahi — D ko alag se check karo.
la-rank-gm-03: $A$ ke diagonal pe $3$ aur baaki sab $1$ hai. $\lambda=2$ ke liye $A-2I$ banao — uski shape bahut simple nikalegi.
GM $=3-\operatorname{rank}(A-2I)$. Diagonal se $2$ ghatao: $A-2I$ ki har entry $1$ ho jaati hai.
All-ones $3\times3$ matrix ki teeno rows same hain — row reduce karke pivots gino, phir $3$ se ghatao. Trap: teen non-zero rows dekh ke rank 3 mat maano, aur rank ko hi GM mat bolo.
la-rank-gm-04: $A$ triangular nahi hai, to diagonal $2,0$ eigenvalues nahi hain. Options eigenvalues aur diagonalizability dono ke baare mein hain — dono check karne padenge.
Char. poly $\lambda^2-(\text{tr})\lambda+\det$: tr $=2$, det $=2\cdot0-(-1)\cdot1=1$. Repeated root mile to GM $=2-\operatorname{rank}(A-\lambda I)$.
$\lambda^2-2\lambda+1=0$ solve karo, phir us $\lambda$ ke liye $A-\lambda I$ likh ke uska rank dekho. Trap: GM ko automatically AM ke barabar maan lena.
la-rank-gm-05: Char. poly se AM mil gaye: $\lambda=1$ aur $\lambda=3$ dono ka AM 2. Diye gaye ranks se GM nikaalna hai, phir har option judge karo.
GM $=n-\operatorname{rank}(A-\lambda I)$ with $n=4$. Invertible iff $0$ eigenvalue nahi hai; $\det A$ = eigenvalues ka product.
GM$(1)=4-\operatorname{rank}(A-I)=4-2$; isi tarah $\lambda=3$ ke liye nikaalo aur har eigenvalue pe GM = AM check karo. Trap: GM ko rank ke barabar mat maano — GM kabhi AM se zyada nahi hota.
la-rank-gm-06: $\lambda=4$ diagonal pe chaar baar hai (AM 4), lekin $(1,2)$ position ka $1$ eigenvectors kam kar deta hai. GM ke liye $A-4I$ ka rank chahiye.
GM $=5-\operatorname{rank}(A-4I)$. Diagonal se $4$ ghatao: last entry $9-4=5$ bachti hai, aur upar wala $1$ bhi.
$A-4I$ ki non-zero rows $(0,1,0,0,0)$ aur $(0,0,0,0,5)$ hain — independent hain ya nahi dekho, rank gino aur $5$ se ghatao. Trap: rank ko hi GM bol dena, ya GM ko AM maan lena.
la-eigvec-check-01: $A$ ki har row ka sum same hai — all-ones vector ke liye yeh bada clue hai. Baaki vectors ke liye $Av$ compute karke proportionality dekho.
$v$ eigenvector iff $Av=\lambda v$ kisi $\lambda$ ke liye ($v\neq0$). Equal row sums $s$ ⇒ $A(1,1,1)^T=s(1,1,1)^T$; yahan $s=2+1+1=4$.
Option B: $A(1,2,0)^T=(2+2,\;1+4,\;1+2)^T$ — ise $(1,2,0)^T$ se compare karo; C ke liye bhi aise hi. Trap: scaled vector $(2,2,2)^T$ ko bhi test karo, ignore mat karo.
la-eigvec-check-02: Rows dekho: $1+2+3$, $3+2+1$, $2+2+2$ — sabka sum same hai. Ek eigenvalue isi se mil jaata hai; baaki do ke liye trace aur det.
Row sum $6$ ⇒ eigenvalue $6$ (eigenvector $(1,1,1)^T$). Phir $\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=\operatorname{tr}A=5$ aur product $=\det A$.
$\det A=1(4-2)-2(6-2)+3(6-4)$ evaluate karo; zero aaye to $0$ ek eigenvalue hai, aur teesra trace se nikaalo. Trap: $0$ milte hi use smallest maan ke ruk jaana.
la-eigvec-check-03: Eigenvalue $2$ diya hai; uska eigenvector $(A-2I)x=0$ ka non-zero solution hai. Options ko $Av=2v$ se seedha bhi check kar sakte ho.
$A-2I=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ — dono rows same, to ek hi equation bachti hai: $2x+y=0$.
$2x+y=0$ mein $x=1$ rakho, $y$ nikaalo aur options se milao; phir $Av$ se verify karo. Trap: $(1,1)^T$ equal row sums wala eigenvector hai — wo $\lambda=5$ ka hai.
la-eigvec-check-04: Har row ka sum $3$ hai — socho $A\mathbf 1$ kya hoga ($\mathbf 1$ = all-ones vector). Har option isi ek fact se judge hota hai.
Row sums $s$ ⇒ $A\mathbf 1=s\mathbf 1$; phir $A^2\mathbf 1=s^2\mathbf 1$ aur $A^{-1}\mathbf 1=\frac1s\mathbf 1$. Kisi matrix $M$ ke row sums = $M\mathbf 1$ ki entries.

$s=3$ rakho: $A^2\mathbf 1=A(3\mathbf 1)$ simplify karo; $A^{-1}$ ke liye $A\mathbf 1=3\mathbf 1$ pe dono taraf $A^{-1}$ lagao. Trap: row sums column sums ke baare mein kuch nahi batate — ek chhota 2×2 example try karo.
la-eigvec-check-05: $(2,1)^T$ eigenvector hona chahiye, yaani $A(2,1)^T$ ko $(2,1)^T$ ka multiple banna hai. Unknown do hain: $k$ aur $\lambda$.
$A(2,1)^T=(2\cdot2+k\cdot1,\;1\cdot2+4\cdot1)^T=(4+k,\,6)^T$, aur yeh $\lambda(2,1)^T=(2\lambda,\lambda)^T$ ke barabar hona chahiye.
Second component se $\lambda=6$ milta hai; ab first component $4+k=2\lambda$ mein daal ke $k$ nikaalo. Trap: $4+k=6$ likhna — first component $\lambda\cdot2$ hona chahiye, sirf $\lambda$ nahi.
la-det-props-06: $n=3$ aur $\det A=2$ fixed hai; har option ek alag rule test karta hai — scalar multiple, inverse, transpose, product.
Rules: $\det(cA)=c^3\det A$, $\det(A^{-1})=1/\det A$, $\det(A^T)=\det A$, aur $\det(XY)=\det X\cdot\det Y$.
Option C: $\det(A^2A^T)=(\det A)^2\cdot\det(A^T)$ — har factor mein $2$ daal ke khud multiply karo. Trap: $\det(cA)=c\det A$ likhna; aur odd $n$ pe $(-1)^3$ sign flip karta hai.
la-det-poly-06: Eigenvalues $1$ aur $3$ diye hain; har option kisi polynomial $p(A)$ ka det, ya khud $p(A)$, ke baare mein hai.
Rule: $\det p(A)=p(1)\cdot p(3)$. Cayley–Hamilton: $A$ apne char. poly $(\lambda-1)(\lambda-3)=\lambda^2-4\lambda+3$ ko satisfy karta hai.
Option D: $p(\lambda)=\lambda+1$ ko $\lambda=1$ aur $\lambda=3$ pe evaluate karke multiply karo, phir $\det A+1$ se compare karo. Trap: determinant additive nahi hota.
la-projection-01: $P^2=P$ aur $P^T=P$ ⇒ orthogonal projection, aur rank $r$ strictly $0$ aur $n$ ke beech hai. Har option ko eigenvalues ki nazar se dekho.
$Pv=\lambda v$ ⇒ $P^2v=\lambda^2v=\lambda v$, to $\lambda^2=\lambda$. Eigenvalue $1$ ki count = rank $r$; $\det$ = eigenvalues ka product, trace = sum.
$r<n$ hai to $n-r$ eigenvalues $0$ hain — ab $\det P$ aur $\operatorname{tr}P$ socho. D ke liye $x=Px+(I-P)x$ likho, dono parts orthogonal hain. Trap: $r<n$ bhool ke $P$ ko $I$ jaisa treat karna.
la-projection-02: Line pe projection: $Px$ hamesha $a$ ka multiple hota hai. Bas coefficient nikaalna hai, phir third component.

$a^Tx=1\cdot3+2\cdot0+2\cdot3$ compute karo, $9$ se divide karo, phir us coefficient ko $a$ ke third component se multiply karo. Trap: $\lVert a\rVert^2$ se divide karna hai, $\lVert a\rVert=3$ se nahi.
la-projection-03: $A$ ke columns $(1,1,1)$ aur $(0,1,-1)$ ka dot product $0$ hai. Orthogonal columns pe projection har column pe alag karke jod sakte ho.
$p=\frac{b^Ta_1}{a_1^Ta_1}a_1+\frac{b^Ta_2}{a_2^Ta_2}a_2$ with $a_1^Ta_1=3$, $a_2^Ta_2=2$. Phir residual $b-p$ ki squared length chahiye.
$b^Ta_1=1+2+4=7$, $b^Ta_2=2-4=-2$; ab $p$ ke components likho aur $b-p$ nikaalo. Trap: $\lVert p\rVert^2$ nahi, residual $\lVert b-p\rVert^2$ chahiye; $a_i^Ta_i$ se divide karna mat bhoolo.
la-projection-04: Sawaal **orthogonal** projection ka hai — sirf idempotent hona kaafi nahi. Har matrix pe do alag test lagane hain.
Orthogonal projection $\iff P^2=P$ aur $P^T=P$. Symmetry aankh se dikh jaati hai; $P^2$ ke liye 2×2 multiply karo.
Option D: $D^T$ likh ke $D$ se compare karo, aur $D^2$ bhi nikaalo; baaki options pe bhi dono test lagao. Trap: in do conditions mein se koi ek akele kaafi nahi.
la-projection-05: $A$ $5\times2$ hai, square nahi — $P=A(A^TA)^{-1}A^T$ uske 2-dim column space pe projection hai. Har option ko dimensions se judge karo.
Projection ka rank = column space ka dimension $=\operatorname{rank}A$; eigenvalue $1$ column space pe, $0$ uske orthogonal complement pe. Trace = rank.
Option C: $PA=A(A^TA)^{-1}(A^TA)$ — beech wala part simplify karo. Trap: $(A^TA)^{-1}=A^{-1}(A^T)^{-1}$ tabhi valid hai jab $A^{-1}$ exist kare — $5\times2$ ke liye check karo.
la-orthogonal-01: Sirf itna pata hai ki $Q^TQ=I$. Har option ko isi ek equation se derive karke dekho.
$\det$ lo: $\det(Q^T)\det Q=1$. Length: $\lVert Qx\rVert^2=x^TQ^TQx$. Eigenvalues ke liye guarantee $|\lambda|$ ki hai, $\lambda$ ki nahi.

Option C test karne ke liye $90^\circ$ rotation $\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ ka char. poly $\lambda^2+1=0$ solve karo. Trap: real orthogonal matrix ke eigenvalues complex bhi ho sakte hain.
la-orthogonal-02: Orthogonal matrix ke columns orthonormal hone chahiye: har column unit length, aur dono perpendicular. Pehla column $(0.6,0.8)$ already unit hai.
Second column $(a,b)$ pe do conditions: $0.6a+0.8b=0$ aur $a^2+b^2=1$.
Option C check karo: $0.6\cdot0.8+0.8\cdot0.6$ zero hai kya? Phir baaki options pe dono conditions lagao. Trap: sirf perpendicular hona kaafi nahi — length bhi $1$ chahiye.
la-orthogonal-03: Orthogonal $Q$ ka $|\det Q|$ hamesha fixed hota hai. $3Q$ mein har row $3$ se scale hui hai, aur matrix $4\times4$ hai.
$|\det(3Q)|=3^4\cdot|\det Q|$ — power evaluate karo. Trap: $3\cdot1$ ya $3\cdot4$ likhna; $c$ ko $n$ ki power pe raise karna hai.
la-orthogonal-04: Orthogonal matrices product, inverse, transpose ke under band hain — par addition ke under? Har option ko $M^TM=I$ test se check karo.
Test: $M$ orthogonal iff $M^TM=I$. D mein $(Q_1Q_2)^T=Q_2^TQ_1^T$ use karo; C mein symmetric ka matlab $Q_1^T=Q_1$.
Option A ke liye simplest example lo: $Q_1=Q_2=I$ — $Q_1+Q_2$ lengths preserve karta hai? C mein $Q_1^2=Q_1^TQ_1$ likh ke socho. Trap: group property ko addition pe bhi laga dena.
la-orthogonal-05: $H=I-2uu^T$ ek reflection (Householder) hai. Trace linear hai, to $I_3$ aur $uu^T$ ka trace alag-alag socho.
$\operatorname{tr}(I_3)=3$ aur $\operatorname{tr}(uu^T)=u^Tu$. Check karo $u=\tfrac13(1,2,2)^T$ unit vector hai ya nahi.
$u^Tu=\tfrac19(1+4+4)$ compute karo, phir $\operatorname{tr}H=3-2\,u^Tu$ mein daalo. Trap: $\det H$ ko trace samajh lena, ya $-2uu^T$ ka trace zero maan lena.
la-definiteness-01: Cross term $4xy$ hai — symmetric matrix banate waqt yeh do off-diagonal entries mein barabar bant jaata hai. Phir definiteness check karo.
Matrix $\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$. 2×2 rule: $a_{11}>0$ aur $\det>0$ ⇒ PD; $\det=0$ ⇒ semidefinite; $\det<0$ ⇒ indefinite.
Pehla minor $3>0$; ab $\det=3\cdot2-2\cdot2$ nikaalo aur rule se match karo. Trap: off-diagonal pe poora $4$ rakhna — cross term halve karna padta hai.
la-definiteness-02: 'PSD but not PD' ka matlab: form kabhi negative nahi, par kisi non-zero $(x,y)$ pe zero — yaani matrix singular. $k$ isi condition se aayega.
Symmetric matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&k\\k&4\end{pmatrix}$ (cross term $2kxy$ halve hua). Condition: $\det=1\cdot4-k^2=0$, saath mein $k>0$.
$4-k^2=0$ solve karo aur positive root lo. Trap: halve na karne se $\begin{pmatrix}1&2k\\2k&4\end{pmatrix}$ banta hai jo galat $k$ deta hai; square root lena mat bhoolo.
la-definiteness-03: $G=A^TA$ Gram matrix hai, size $n\times n$. Har option ko $x^TGx=\lVert Ax\rVert^2$ ki nazar se socho.
$x^TGx=\lVert Ax\rVert^2\ge0$, zero tabhi jab $Ax=0$. PD ke liye $Ax=0$ ka sirf $x=0$ solution chahiye; aur $\operatorname{rank}G=\operatorname{rank}A\le\min(m,n)$.
Option D: $m<n$ ho to $\operatorname{rank}A\le m<n$ — kya $Ax=0$ ka non-zero solution banega? C ke liye $A^TAv=\lambda v$ pe dono taraf $A$ lagao. Trap: Gram matrix ko hamesha PD maan lena.
la-definiteness-04: $A$ symmetric tridiagonal hai (diagonal $2$, off-diagonal $-1$). Definiteness leading minors ya eigenvalues se decide hoti hai, off-diagonal ke sign se nahi.
Leading minors: $D_1=2$, $D_2=2\cdot2-(-1)(-1)$, $D_3=\det A$. Symmetric matrix ke liye: sab minors $>0$ ⇔ PD ⇔ sab eigenvalues $>0$.
$D_2=3$; ab $\det A=2(4-1)-(-1)\cdot\det\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ evaluate karo. Trap: diagonal ka product det nahi hai — $A$ triangular nahi hai.
la-definiteness-05: PD ke liye positive entries ya positive diagonal kaafi nahi. Har 2×2 symmetric matrix pe ek hi chhota test lagao.
2×2 symmetric: PD iff $a_{11}>0$ aur $\det>0$. $\det=0$ ho to sirf semidefinite, $\det<0$ ho to indefinite.
Option B: $\det=4\cdot2-3\cdot3$ nikaalo aur sign dekho; baaki options ka det bhi isi tarah. Trap: 'saari entries positive hain to PD' — yeh galat shortcut hai.
la-rayleigh-01: Unit vectors pe $x^TAx$ ka maximum Rayleigh quotient ka max hai — yeh matrix ke ek khaas number ke barabar hota hai, kisi diagonal entry ke nahi.
Max $=\lambda_{\max}(A)$. 2×2 ke liye $\lambda^2-(\text{tr})\lambda+\det=0$; yahan tr $=6$, det $=9-1=8$.
$\lambda^2-6\lambda+8=0$ factor karo aur bada root lo. Trap: $x=(1,1)^T$ seedha mat daalo — wo unit vector nahi hai ($\lVert x\rVert^2=2$).
la-rayleigh-02: Constraint $x^2+y^2=1$ ⇒ unit circle pe quadratic form ka minimum, yaani Rayleigh quotient. Pehle form ka symmetric matrix banao.
Matrix $\begin{pmatrix}5&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$ ($4xy$ halve hoke $2,2$). Minimum $=\lambda_{\min}$; tr $=7$, det $=10-4=6$.
$\lambda^2-7\lambda+6=0$ factor karo aur chhota root lo. Trap: chhota diagonal coefficient $2$ minimum nahi hai — wo sirf $(0,1)$ pe value hai.
la-rayleigh-03: Eigenvalues $-2,1,5$ diye hain; $R(x)$ ki range inhi se decide hoti hai. Option C mein $\lVert x\rVert\le2$ hai, unit sphere nahi — wahan dhyan.
Rule: $\lambda_{\min}\le R(x)\le\lambda_{\max}$, extremes eigenvectors pe milte hain. Aur $x^TAx=R(x)\,\lVert x\rVert^2$.

Option C: $\lVert x\rVert=2$ pe $x^TAx=4\,R(x)$ — ab max $R$ se multiply karke $10$ se compare karo. D: $\lambda=1$ ka eigenvector daal ke socho. Trap: $\lVert x\rVert$ se scale karna, $\lVert x\rVert^2$ ke bajaye.
la-rayleigh-04: $A$ diagonal hai, to $x^TAx=2x_1^2-3x_2^2+x_3^2$ seedha likh sakte ho. Sawaal max ka hai — sign ke saath, absolute value nahi.
Symmetric $A$: $\max_{\lVert x\rVert=1}x^TAx=\lambda_{\max}$. Diagonal matrix ke eigenvalues = diagonal entries $2,-3,1$.
Constraint $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1$ hai; socho poora weight kis coordinate pe daalne se $2x_1^2-3x_2^2+x_3^2$ sabse bada hoga. Trap: $|-3|$ bada dikhta hai, par $-3x_2^2$ value ghatata hai.
la-rayleigh-05: Unit circle pe $f(x)=x^TAx$ ke extremes $A$ ke eigenvalues hain, aur eigenvectors pe milte hain. Har option mein value aur location dono check karo.
Row sums equal hain ⇒ $(1,1)^T$ eigenvector, eigenvalue = row sum. Doosra eigenvalue trace $4$ se nikaalo; uska eigenvector $(1,-1)^T$ hai.
$A(1,-1)^T=(2-1,\;1-2)^T$ compute karke eigenvalue dekho, phir socho wo min hai ya max. Trap: diagonal entries sirf $f(e_i)$ ki values hain — unhe automatically min/max mat maano.
la-lu-01: Doolittle LU: $L$ ke diagonal pe $1$, aur $U$ = elimination ke baad bachi rows. $u_{22}$ = row 2 ki second entry, elimination ke baad.
$l_{21}=3$; ab $R_2-3R_1$ karo aur uski second entry dekho. Trap: subtract ki jagah add karna, ya bina eliminate kiye $a_{22}$ copy kar dena.
la-lu-02: $u_{33}$ elimination ke bilkul end mein milta hai — row 3 ko pehle row 1 se aur phir naye row 2 se reduce karna padega.
$R_2-2R_1=(0,1,1)$, to $u_{22}=1$ aur $l_{32}=3/1=3$. Ab $R_3-3\cdot(0,1,1)$ karo aur last entry dekho. Trap: $a_{33}=4$ copy karna — row 3 abhi reduce karni baaki hai.
la-lu-03: Sawaal **no** LU (bina row exchange) ka hai. LU tab fail hota hai jab pivot zero ho aur uske neeche non-zero entry ho — singular hona alag baat hai.
Doolittle mein $u_{11}=a_{11}$ aur $l_{21}u_{11}=a_{21}$. Agar $a_{11}=0$ par $a_{21}\neq0$, to yeh equation satisfy hi nahi ho sakti.
Har option ka $a_{11}$ aur $a_{21}$ dekho; D ke liye $l_{21}=1$ leke $u_{22}=1-1\cdot1$ nikaalo — factorization bana ya nahi? Trap: singular matrix ka matlab 'LU nahi' maan lena.
la-lu-04: $A=LU$ given hai, $L$ unit lower triangular. Har option ko $\det L$, triangular solves aur zero pivot ke angle se dekho.
$\det A=\det L\cdot\det U$ with $\det L=1$, aur triangular ka det = diagonal product. $Ax=b$ ⇒ $L(Ux)=b$; $y=Ux$ rakho.

Option A ke liye ek invertible matrix lo jiska $a_{11}=0$ ho, jaise $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ — bina row swap ke pehla pivot milta hai? Trap: invertible ko 'LU without pivoting possible' maan lena.
la-lu-05: $A=LU$ ki sirf $(3,3)$ entry chahiye, poora product nahi. Yeh $L$ ki row 3 aur $U$ ke column 3 ka dot product hai.
Pehla term $(-1)(1)=-1$; ab $3\cdot(-1)$ aur $1\cdot4$ nikaal ke teeno jodo. Trap: sirf $l_{33}u_{33}$ lena, ya $u_{23}=-1$ ka sign bhoolna.
la-lu-06: 2×2 LU mein ek hi elimination step hai. Options $u_{22}$, $\det A$ aur $l_{21}$ ke baare mein hain — ek baar eliminate karke sab check ho jaayenge.
$l_{21}=3/1$; ab $u_{22}=4-l_{21}\cdot2$ nikaalo aur $\det A=1\cdot4-2\cdot3$ se cross-check karo. Trap: subtract ki jagah add karna.
la-svd-01: Singular values $A$ ke eigenvalues nahi hote — yahan $A$ triangular hai par symmetric nahi. Inke liye $A^TA$ chahiye.
$A^TA=\begin{pmatrix}25&20\\20&25\end{pmatrix}$; equal row sums se ek eigenvalue $25+20$, doosra $25-20$. Bade wale ka square root lo. Trap: diagonal $5$ ko le lena, ya square root bhoolna.
la-svd-02: $A=uv^T$ rank-one outer product hai ($3\times2$). Rank-one matrix ka sirf ek non-zero singular value hota hai — socho wo kis se banta hai.
$uv^T$ ka non-zero singular value $=\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert$. $A^TA=\lVert u\rVert^2vv^T$, eigenvalues $\lVert u\rVert^2\lVert v\rVert^2$ aur $0$.
$\lVert u\rVert=\sqrt{1+4+4}$, $\lVert v\rVert=\sqrt{9+16}$ nikaalo, phir A aur D ko inke product se check karo. Trap: dono norms ko alag-alag singular values maan lena.
la-svd-03: Har option singular values ka ek alag rule test karta hai: symmetric PSD, max stretch, rank, aur negative eigenvalue wala case.
$\sigma_i=\sqrt{\lambda_i(A^TA)}\ge0$. Symmetric $A$ ke liye $A^TA=A^2$, to $\sigma=|\lambda|$. Rank = non-zero $\sigma$ ki count.
Option D: $A^2$ ke eigenvalues $3^2$ aur $(-2)^2$ ke square roots lo aur compare karo; C mein non-zero singular values gino. Trap: singular value ko negative ho sakne wala maan lena.
la-svd-04: Saari entries ke squares ka sum = Frobenius norm$^2$. Matrix nahi diya, sirf singular values — to dono ko jodne wali identity chahiye.
Singular values $3,2,1$ ko square karo ($3^2=9$, …) aur add karo. Trap: bina square kiye add karna, ya poore sum ko square karna.
la-svd-05: $A$ ke dono columns same hain, $(1,1,0)$ — to rank kitna hoga? Singular values $A^TA$ se aayenge.
$\sigma_i=\sqrt{\lambda_i(A^TA)}$. $A^TA$ ki $(i,j)$ entry = column $i$ · column $j$; yahan har dot product $1+1+0=2$.
$A^TA=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$ ke eigenvalues trace aur det se nikaalo, phir square root lo. Trap: $A^TA$ ke eigenvalues ko hi singular values likh dena.
la-svd-06: General $m\times n$, rank $r$ matrix hai. Har option ko is fact se judge karo ki singular values $A^TA$ se aate hain, $A$ ke char. poly se nahi.
$\sigma_i^2=\lambda_i(A^TA)$, $\operatorname{rank}(A^TA)=\operatorname{rank}A$, $\lVert Ax\rVert^2=x^TA^TAx\le\sigma_1^2\lVert x\rVert^2$; $A^TA$ aur $AA^T$ ke non-zero eigenvalues same.

Option A ko $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ pe test karo: eigenvalues diagonal se, singular values $A^TA$ banake — phir compare. Trap: $\sigma=|\lambda|$ sirf symmetric (normal) matrices ke liye hai.
